what: query-unify asks for a port window (Andrew 14:22: delete salsa). The engine blaze_query::db and blaze-query-macros now check (cargo check -p blaze-query -p blaze-query-macros); their tests finish within the hour. The port cannot keep every save compiling across crates: once base-db s inputs and ids are blaze_query ones, every crate above that still says #[salsa::tracked] over them fails until it is ported (no bridge: a salsa shim is forbidden). So: hand query-unify (child query-unify-port and its children) span, intern, base-db, hir-expand, hir-def, hir-ty, hir-ty-mir, hir-ty-codegen, hir-ty-borrowck, hir-ty-wfcheck, hir-ty-* others, blaze-items, blaze-item-hash, hir-firewall, hir, blaze-lints, blaze-lower, blaze-macro-*, blaze-cargo s salsa uses, and the ~22 small crates naming salsa (rg -l salsa crates/*/Cargo.toml), held together from when you say go until each checks. During the window, errors in a crate above the one being ported are expected; the port goes bottom-up and each crate checks clean (cargo check -p) before the next. Other lanes fixing compile errors there should stop or queue their edits to query-unify-port for the window. Tell me (tmux query-unify-next1 or queue) when, and whether you want it sooner or after the current check loop reaches zero.
